text:
- [LCDB.7.2] **Suppression is keyed on `(rule, activation_key)`, and there is
  no `global` modifier.** The grammar offers no rule-wide variant to write.

  ⚠ **Rule-wide suppression is nevertheless REACHABLE, with no modifier and no
  author opt-in.** A schema with no `key` slot — the default for a schema
  written without identity in mind — gives **every** activation the empty
  activation key, so `(rule, [])` is one window for the whole rule.

  **The grammar claim holds.** No `global` modifier exists, so nothing here is
  spellable; what an author gets instead is the behaviour arriving as a
  consequence of the schema they wrote. The logical-fact sentinel is a way to
  express rule-wide suppression deliberately, and not the only way to reach it.

  The behaviour stands, and because an author who never chose a key never chose
  a rule-wide window either, the compiler says so ([LCDB.7.9]).

idris.name: lcdb_3_3_3__every_activation_shares_one_key
idris.note: Establishes the clause: a schema with no `key` slot — the default for a schema written without identity in mind — gives every activation the empty activation key, so `(rule, [])` is one window for the whole rule, which is the reachable rule-wide suppression the clause states. The lemma's force is the reading that suppression is keyed on `(rule, activation_key)`; the equation `[] = []` is what makes that reading checkable by anyone with `[LCDB.3.3.3]` and this clause in front of them.
